classification.difficultyReason: Use several parallel-line and triangle relationships in two compound diagrams.

content.prompt: Determine the sizes of the unknown angles where possible. If individual angles cannot be determined, state a relationship between them.

spec.description: Three descending parallel lines, a near-vertical transversal and a diagonal forming the lower triangle; retain all ten unknown labels.
spec.mathematics: Givens 108° and 130°; matching single-arrow parallel markers.

answer.short: $a=72^\circ,\ b=108^\circ,\ c=72^\circ,\ d=72^\circ,\ e=108^\circ,\ f=72^\circ,\ g=50^\circ,\ h=50^\circ,\ i=58^\circ,\ j=72^\circ$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}a+108&=180\\a&=72^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line give $a=72^\circ$. Vertically opposite angles give $b=108^\circ$ and $c=a=72^\circ$. Corresponding angles give $d=c=72^\circ$, $e=b=108^\circ$, $f=a=72^\circ$ and $j=c=72^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}g+130&=180\\g&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line give $g=50^\circ$. Alternate angles give $h=g=50^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}i+50+72&=180\\i+122&=180\\i&=58^\circ\end{align*}$$
The interior angles of the lower triangle sum to $180^\circ$.

spec.description: ABCD with only AB and DC marked parallel; E lies on DB and EC is drawn.
spec.mathematics: DAB=110°, ADB=28°, BEC=47°. No source condition establishes AD parallel to BC.
spec.answerVisibility: All six pronumerals remain unsolved; no additional parallel condition.

answer.short: $a=42^\circ,\ b=42^\circ,\ e=133^\circ,\ f=5^\circ$. The given information determines $c+d=133^\circ$, but does not determine $c$ and $d$ separately.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ADB$:
$$\begin{align*}a+110+28&=180\\a+138&=180\\a&=42^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $AB\parallel DC$, alternate angles give $b=a=42^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}e+47&=180\\e&=133^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on the straight line $DB$ give $e=133^\circ$. In $\triangle DEC$:
$$\begin{align*}f+42+133&=180\\f+175&=180\\f&=5^\circ\end{align*}$$
In $\triangle BEC$:
$$\begin{align*}c+d+47&=180\\c+d&=133^\circ\end{align*}$$
The source does not establish $AD\parallel BC$, so $c$ and $d$ cannot be found separately. If that additional condition is supplied, alternate angles give $c=28^\circ$ and then $d=105^\circ$.
